DISCOVERY.question: What are the top-level service directories in the CMR repository and what does each do?
DISCOVERY.answer: The CMR repository contains eight deployable services: (1) search-app — public REST/STAC/AQL search API backed by Elasticsearch; (2) ingest-app — provider-facing metadata ingest, validates UMM, stores via metadata-db, triggers indexing; (3) indexer-app — consumes ingest events from SQS, transforms concepts, writes to Elasticsearch; (4) metadata-db-app — Oracle-backed durable concept store with versioned history; (5) access-control-app — ACL groups and permission management stored in Elasticsearch; (6) bootstrap-app — bulk migration and reindex utility; (7) virtual-product-app — derives virtual granule records from source products; (8) mock-echo-app — stub ECHO/URS service for local dev and integration tests. A Python subscription worker in /subscription polls SQS and fans notifications out to SNS. All services share a set of libraries under directories ending in -lib.
DISCOVERY.evidence: project.clj :modules :dirs lists all apps; README.md describes each; dev-system/src/cmr/dev_system/system.clj app-control-functions and app-startup-order enumerate them

DISCOVERY.question: What libraries are shared across CMR services?
DISCOVERY.answer: Shared libraries (all under nasa-cmr group): cmr-common-lib (lifecycle, config, concepts, generics, caching), cmr-common-app-lib (Ring middleware, humanizers, search protocol), cmr-umm-spec-lib (UMM parsers/converters/validators), cmr-umm-lib (legacy UMM), cmr-elastic-utils-lib (Elasticsearch query building and index management), cmr-message-queue-lib (SQS/SNS abstraction), cmr-transmit-lib (typed HTTP clients for inter-service calls), cmr-spatial-lib (geodetic/cartesian geometry, orbit intersection), cmr-acl-lib (ACL fetcher and enforcement), cmr-oracle-lib (Oracle JDBC pool), cmr-redis-utils-lib (Redis cache), cmr-schema-validation-lib (JSON Schema), cmr-orbits-lib (satellite orbit math), cmr-schemas (JSON Schema files for generic document types).

DISCOVERY.question: What are the top-level non-service directories and what is their purpose?
DISCOVERY.answer: .clj-kondo/ — static analysis config; .github/workflows/ — CI via cmr-checks.yml; bin/ — cmr CLI tool with bash autocomplete; dev-system/ — single-process dev harness embedding all services; other/ — miscellaneous scripts; resources/ — shell autocomplete and shared templates; schemas/ — JSON Schema files for generic document types; site-templates/ — shared HTML templates (gov.nasa.earthdata/cmr-site-templates artifact); system-int-test/ — cross-service integration tests; search-relevancy-test/ — relevancy scoring benchmarks.
DISCOVERY.evidence: Root directory listing via gh api repos/.../contents/; README.md; project.clj :modules :dirs

DISCOVERY.question: What concept types does CMR manage?
DISCOVERY.answer: CMR manages: collection (UMM-C), granule (UMM-G), service (UMM-S), tool (UMM-T), subscription (UMM-Sub), variable (UMM-Var), tag, tag-association, group, acl, service-association, tool-association, variable-association, generic-association. It also supports a set of extensible generic document types (grid, data-quality-summary, order-option, visualization, citation — and their -draft variants) governed by the approved-pipeline-documents configuration. Each concept type has a unique ID prefix (e.g., C for collection, G for granule, GRD for grid).
DISCOVERY.evidence: common-lib/src/cmr/common/concepts.clj (generic-concept-types->concept-prefix map, draft detection); umm-spec-lib/src/cmr/umm_spec/umm_spec_core.clj (concept-type dispatch on UMM record types); metadata-db-app/src/cmr/metadata_db/data/oracle/concepts/ directory (per-type Oracle implementations); schemas/resources/schemas/ directory listing
